    .Where(u => u.Age > 18)
    .OrderBy(u => u.Name)
    .Select(u => new { u.Name, u.Age })

dbContext.Users
    .Where(u => u.Age >= 18)
    .GroupBy(u => u.Role)
    .Where(g => g.Count() > 1)
    .Select(g => new { Role = g.Key, Cnt = g.Count() })
    .OrderByDescending(x => x.Cnt)

context.Users
    .Where(u => u.Age >= 25)
    .GroupJoin(context.Orders,
        u => u.Id,
        o => o.Owner,
        (u, orders) => new { u, orders })
    .SelectMany(
        x => x.orders.DefaultIfEmpty(),
        (x, o) => new { Name = x.u.Name, Item = o != null ? o.Item : null })
    .OrderByDescending(r => r.Name)
    .Take(4)

context.Users
    .Where(u => context.Orders.Any(o => o.Owner == u.Id))
    .Select(u => new { u.Name, Level = u.Age > 40 ? "Senior" : u.Age > 25 ? "Mid" : "Junior" })
    .OrderBy(x => x.Name)

context.Users
    .Where(u => EF.Functions.Like(u.Name, "B%"))
    .Join(context.Orders, u => u.Id, o => o.Owner, (u, o) => new { u, o })
    .Join(context.Products, uo => uo.o.Id, p => p.Parent, (uo, p) => new { uo.u, uo.o, p })
    .Where(x => x.o.Qty >= 1 || x.p.Price < 20)
    .OrderByDescending(x => x.p.Price)
    .Skip(1)
    .Take(5)
    .Select(x => new { x.u.Name, x.o.Item, x.p.Title })
